column1: # DEV-d: databases (db), HTTP (api), local CI (ci), forge dashboards (forge). Format: see the header of ~/.config/hub/hub.

column9: Connections of this project ([db.NAME] in .envs.toml), of the other bound projects and of the global scope, plus running DB containers without a config. Enter opens lazysql (MariaDB, MySQL, Postgres, SQLite, ClickHouse native); docker ports are resolved at every start; a protected environment opens read-only. Keys: r read-only, e environment, c client inside the container, a add, E edit, y copy the URL without the password, s start a stopped container. Passwords come from Bitwarden through envs and are never on screen, argv or in a file. tmux prefix b opens it in the pane's directory.

posting on the project's api/ collection with the env files api/env/base.env + <env>.env of the active environment; the declared secrets are available as ${NAME} in a request (from Bitwarden through envs, nothing written). posting runs with a scrubbed environment and no history. Outside a project it opens the scratch collection. tmux prefix a opens it in the pane's directory. `api init` creates the skeleton.

hurl --test over api/tests/**/*.hurl of this project with the secrets as HURL_SECRET_<NAME> (redacted in logs and reports) and the plain variables of api/env/*.env. Run it from the project directory; `api test FILE --report` writes an HTML report to api/tests/report/.

Lists the jobs of the repository's GitHub workflows (act) or .gitlab-ci.yml (gitlab-ci-local) and runs one, everything, or a dry run. Only the secrets named in [ci] of .envs.toml are passed (Bitwarden through envs). gitlab-ci-local jobs without an image run ON THIS MACHINE (key i switches to containers); act pulls a 1-2 GB image on its first run (asks once).

The dashboard of the repository's forge: gh-dash for github.com (gh's own login), glab-tui for any other host (GITLAB_TOKEN and GITLAB_HOST from Bitwarden Env/global through `envs run -g`). Outside a repository it asks which dashboard.
glab ci view in the current repository with the GitLab token from Bitwarden (Env/global); no glab login or config is involved.
